turns.prompt_text: Good evening, I am trying to get github to clone locally, I have created an ssh key in the .ssh folder on my mac mini and placed the public key in github
turns.response_html:
Good evening. It sounds like you have done the hardest parts (generating the key and adding it to GitHub).

If the clone is failing or asking for a password, it is usually because the Mac's SSH agent hasn't loaded the key yet, or you are using the HTTPS URL instead of the SSH URL.

Here is the step-by-step to get it working on your Mac Mini.

1. Test the Connection

First, run this command in your terminal to see if GitHub recognizes you.

ssh -T git@github.com
  • If it says: Hi [username]! You've successfully authenticated...
    • The Fix: You are likely using the wrong URL style. Skip to Step 4.
  • If it says: Permission denied (publickey).
    • The Fix: Your computer isn't offering the key to GitHub. Proceed to Step 2.

2. Add the Key to the SSH Agent

On macOS, you must explicitly tell the SSH agent to manage your key.

Run this command (replace id_ed25519 with your actual key name, e.g., id_rsa, if you used the default legacy format):

ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Note: If you are on an older version of macOS (pre-Monterey), use -K instead of --apple-use-keychain.

3. Ensure the Agent Loads Automatically (Optional but Recommended)

To prevent having to run the command in Step 2 every time you restart your Mac, you should create a config file.

  1. Check if a config file exists: open ~/.ssh/config
  2. If it doesn't exist, create it: touch ~/.ssh/config
  3. Open it in a text editor and paste this in:
Host github.com
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

(Again, ensure the filename matches your actual key).

4. Clone Using the SSH URL

This is the most common point of confusion. You cannot use the standard https:// link if you want to use SSH keys.

  1. Go to the repository on GitHub.
  2. Click the green Code button.
  3. Select the SSH tab (ensure it starts with git@).
  4. Run the clone command:
git clone git@github.com:username/repository-name.git

Did the ssh -T git@github.com command return the "Hi!" success message for you?
